record.paper_title: The Projection Technique for Two Open Problems of Unconstrained Optimization Problems
record.context_brief: Alternative boundary conditions for projection methods
record.original_question: In projection-based variants of unconstrained optimization methods that classify iterates into in-points and out-points using a boundary condition, are there boundary conditions other than the one used in this paper that can effectively separate the in-points from the out-points?

evidence.quote: Are there other conditions such as the boundary to separate the in-points and the out-points?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an iterative algorithm for the unconstrained optimization problem

   minimize f(x),  x ∈ ℝⁿ,

where f : ℝⁿ → ℝ is continuously differentiable (and, where needed, twice continuously differentiable). A projection-based variant of such an algorithm (for example, a Polak–Ribière–Polyak conjugate-gradient method or a BFGS quasi-Newton method under a weak Wolfe–Powell line search) generates a sequence of iterates {xₖ} together with search directions {dₖ} and step lengths {αₖ}, and classifies each iterate xₖ as an "in-point" or an "out-point" according to a chosen scalar boundary condition B(xₖ, dₖ, ∇f(xₖ), …) ⋛ 0. In-points are kept as ordinary iterates, while out-points are replaced by a projection step designed to restore descent and to guarantee global convergence (including in nonconvex settings, where standard examples show that circle-type cycling can occur).

A particular boundary condition has been used in such a projection scheme to separate the in-points from the out-points and to ensure global convergence under the weak Wolfe–Powell line search. The problem is the following:

Determine whether there exist boundary conditions, essentially different from the one just described, that

  (i) partition the iterates into in-points and out-points in such a way that the resulting projection-based modification of the algorithm is well-defined,
  (ii) preserve sufficient descent and the standard step-length and direction properties of the underlying method, and
  (iii) yield global convergence of the algorithm for general (possibly nonconvex) continuously differentiable objective functions f under the weak Wolfe–Powell line search.

Exhibit such an alternative boundary condition explicitly and prove the corresponding convergence theorem, or otherwise characterize the class of admissible boundary conditions that can effectively separate the in-points from the out-points in this projection framework.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search returns the paper that introduces the projection technique and its specific boundary condition for separating in-points and out-points to obtain global convergence of PRP and BFGS under the weak Wolfe–Powell line search, but no subsequent work was found that provides or rules out essentially different boundary conditions answering this question. The status therefore appears unresolved in the literature surfaced by the search.

status_evidence.title: The Projection Technique for Two Open Problems of Unconstrained Optimization Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Two problems for nonconvex functions under the weak Wolfe–Powell line search: global convergence of the PRP conjugate gradient algorithm and of the BFGS quasi-Newton method; a projection technique with a boundary condition separating in-points and out-points is introduced.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the original projection framework and the specific boundary condition; no alternative boundary conditions are provided.

status_evidence.title: An Orthogonal Projection Algorithm for ...
status_evidence.snippet: Orthogonal-projection-type algorithms for optimization, without addressing the in-point/out-point boundary-condition question raised in the projection technique framework.
status_evidence.claim: Related projection algorithms exist but do not answer the specific question about alternative separating boundary conditions.
